en.subtitle: Universal Project Blueprint — understanding directories, system components, build lifecycles, and cross-runtime executions for both Java and Kotlin.
en.s1_intro: An Android project is divided into logical modules. In a standard single-module architecture, the default app/ directory contains all the logic assets, source code targets, and deployment configuration parameters.
en.s2_intro: The AndroidManifest.xml is the ultimate ledger file read by the Android OS before booting your software package. Regardless of language choice, you must register hardware permissions and structural views here.
en.s3_intro: The res/ directory houses non-code visual components. During the build workflow, the build system automatically generates a unique tracking file named R.java, turning asset pathways into static integer addresses referenced by your logic code.
en.s4_intro: Android utilizes **Gradle** to orchestrate source code file compilation, dependency downloading, and final code signing processes. Modern configurations use Kotlin Script (.gradle.kts) or Groovy (.gradle).
en.s5_intro: Unlike standard desktop software execution loops, the Android system controls process memory allocations directly. Visual containers called **Activities** travel along a strict state path to adapt smoothly to device interruptions.
en.s6_intro: An application system interaction layer is constructed by utilizing varying combinations of the **Four Fundamental Component Elements** managed directly by the Android OS runtime layer.
en.s7_intro: Android runs all interface drawing operations on a single, isolated execution track known as the **Main Thread** (or UI Thread). Forcing network requests or file modifications onto this track locks up the UI, triggering an immediate app freeze.
en.s8_intro: Whether you choose to write your app logic in Java or Kotlin, both toolchains emit standard JVM instructions. A secondary compilation phase then compresses these bytecode files into custom register configurations optimized for mobile devices.

it.s1_intro: Un progetto Android è suddiviso in moduli logici. In un'applicazione standard a modulo singolo, quasi tutto il lavoro di sviluppo risiede nella directory app/.
it.s2_intro: AndroidManifest.xml è il registro fondamentale letto dal sistema operativo prima di avviare il processo dell'app.
it.s3_intro: La directory res/ ospita i componenti visivi non di codice. Durante la compilazione, il build tools genera una classe statica interna denominata R.
it.s4_intro: Android utilizza Gradle per orchestrare la compilazione del codice sorgente, l'inclusione delle risorse esterne e la gestione dei manifest.
it.s5_intro: A differenza del software desktop tradizionale, il sistema operativo Android può distruggere e ricreare le Activity in qualsiasi momento.
it.s6_intro: L'interazione con il sistema Android si basa su quattro pilastri fondamentali dell'applicazione: Activity, Service, BroadcastReceiver e ContentProvider.
it.s7_intro: Android esegue tutte le operazioni di rendering su un singolo thread principale (UI Thread). I task pesanti devono essere delegati in background.
it.s8_intro: Sia che tu scriva la logica in Java o in Kotlin, entrambi i linguaggi vengono compilati in bytecode DEX ed eseguiti dalla Android Runtime (ART).

es.s1_intro: Un proyecto de Android se divide en módulos lógicos. En una aplicación estándar de módulo único, casi todo el desarrollo reside en el directorio app/.
es.s2_intro: AndroidManifest.xml es el registro fundamental que lee el sistema operativo Android antes de iniciar el proceso de la aplicación.
es.s3_intro: El directorio res/ aloja componentes visuales que no son código. Durante la compilación se genera una clase estática llamada R.
es.s4_intro: Android utiliza Gradle para coordinar la compilación del código fuente, incluir bibliotecas externas y ensamblar paquetes APK/AAB.
es.s5_intro: A diferencia del software de escritorio clásico, el sistema Android puede destruir y recrear Activities en cualquier momento según la memoria.
es.s6_intro: La arquitectura de interacción de Android se construye sobre cuatro componentes esenciales: Activity, Service, BroadcastReceiver y ContentProvider.
es.s7_intro: Android ejecuta el dibujo de interfaz en un único hilo principal (UI Thread). Las tareas pesadas deben delegarse a trabajadores en segundo plano.
es.s8_intro: Ya sea que escribas en Java o Kotlin, el código se compila a bytecode DEX y es ejecutado de forma nativa por el entorno Android Runtime (ART).
